newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans end down on fund sales, weather.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans end down on fund sales, weather.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures ended lower Monday, under pressure from technically-inspired fund sales and favorable weather in South America, traders said.
"We had a poor performance on Friday, and that influenced trade today (Monday)," said one floor trader.
Some traders also linked Monday's weak market to ideas that rain in Argentina has boosted soy output prospects there.
Pressure also stemmed from nearly ideal harvest weather in Brazil's southern soybean growing regions, traders said.
Weather there is expected to remain dry through the end of the week, independent Brazlian meteorologist, Somar said.
Expectations for the U.S. Department of Agriculture to show a strong jump in U.S. soybean plantings in its report on Monday also weighed on the market, CBOT traders said.

""There are ideas the (soy) acreage is edging higher from earlier expectations," said Robert Lekberg, analyst with Goldenberg Hehmeyer in Chicago. "Sixty-seven million acres now is a pretty popular figure."
CBOT soybeans ended down five to 10-3/4 cents per bushel, with May down 10-3/4 at $8.31-3/4 a bushel and July down 9-3/4 at $8.32-3/4.
Shipment data from the U.S. Department of Agriculture also contributed to the market's weak tone, traders and analysts said.
"Exports were lighter than expected in the case of soybeans and that added a little weight to the market," Lekberg said.
USDA put weekly export inspections at 13.775, which fell below trade estimates ranging from 16 to 22 million bushels.

On the day, ADM sold two million bushels May, and Cargill Investor Services sold two million May and 500,000 July. Refco sold 2.5 million May and Griffin trading sold two million July, floor sources said.
In options trade, Term Commodities sold 400 May $8.75 calls and Cargill Investor Services bought 200 July $8.25 calls and sold 200 July $10.00 calls.
Volume was estimated by CBOT at 55,000 contracts, compared with Friday's actual volume of 65,684 contracts.
